requisor.verdict: Applied-AI company that builds task-automation software for teams.
overview: Requisor is an applied-AI company whose software automates repetitive operational work for teams. FutureTools listed it as an intelligent project management tool, but its current public site positions it more broadly as an applied-AI business, so the record follows the current identity. It is a paid product aimed at organizations looking to offload routine workflows. Details beyond the official site were not independently verifiable.

ResolveAI is a Toronto-based platform for building ChatGPT-powered customer-service chatbots trained on your business data. It offers a free plan with paid tiers from about $24/month, aimed at SMBs automating support.
pros: Free plan available
Quick setup
Affordable paid tiers
cons: Quality depends on data
Small vendor
Crowded market

reworkd.verdict: No-code web scraper that generates self-healing extractors and runs them at scale.
overview: Reworkd is a no-code web scraping platform that generates AI-powered extractors and runs them end to end at scale. Its self-healing scrapers adapt when website structures change, handling pagination, dynamic content, retries, rate limits, proxies and captcha solving automatically. A free Hobby plan includes API access and scheduled jobs; Pro starts at $99 per month with more concurrent browsers and longer retention.
pros: Free Hobby tier includes API access and scheduled jobs
Self-healing extractors cut the biggest cost in scraping — maintenance
Fast setup with no code or scraper engineering needed
Fully managed infrastructure with analytics monitoring
cons: Free tier caps data retention at 30 days
Anti-bot protections on some target sites remain a constraint
Small user review base compared to established scraping tools

rezolve-ai.verdict: Agentic AI service desk that autonomously resolves IT, HR and Finance employee requests.
overview: Rezolve.ai is an agentic AI service desk for IT, HR and Finance teams. Its autonomous agents resolve employee issues before they become tickets, assist human agents, and identify what to automate next — all running on a built-in ITSM system of record that can work standalone or alongside existing ticketing tools. The platform emphasizes governed, glass-box automation with SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and HIPAA-ready compliance, and was named in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Applications in ITSM.
pros: 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant recognition for AI applications in ITSM
Resolves issues in ~10 minutes with a significant share never becoming tickets
Enterprise-grade compliance stack for regulated organizations
Proven at scale — e.g. 100,000 employees served at JLL
cons: Enterprise sales-led pricing — no public self-serve plans
Service-desk focus means customer-facing support use cases are secondary
Adoption depends on integration quality with existing ticketing systems

riku-ai.verdict: No-code platform for building custom LLM apps.
overview: Riku.ai lets non-developers build custom AI apps on top of large language models without code: pick a model, design prompts and publish. Freemium plans run $29 and $49 per month with API access. Good for rapid internal tool building.
pros: Fast prototyping
No coding needed
Model flexibility
cons: Paid tiers for serious use
Limited complex logic

rippletide.verdict: Action runtime that checks AI agent actions against your business rules
overview: Rippletide has pivoted to become an action runtime for AI agents — a governance layer that checks what an agent proposes to do against your business rules before anything executes. As agents move from demos to production, the risk is an agent taking a wrong or unauthorized action; Rippletide sits in that gap. It gives teams a way to let agents act autonomously while keeping guardrails enforceable.
pros: Addresses a real gap in agent deployments
Policy-based control without killing autonomy
Free tier to evaluate
cons: New product — track record and integrations still maturing
Pricing details not fully public

ritto.verdict: Show it once and Ritto repeats it: an AI workflow agent that learns routine tasks from one demonstration, with human review gates.
overview: Ritto is an AI workflow agent for recurring work. Show it a real operation once and it records your steps, identifies what changes between iterations, and turns the demonstration into a reusable, reviewable task. Before each run you review the scope and key actions, confirm the risky steps, and Ritto completes the rest the same way every time.
pros: No technical knowledge needed — automation by demonstration
Reviewable before execution with human-in-the-loop for risky steps
Ideal for clear-scope repeat work like resume screening, order checks and batch data entry
cons: Still in early development / beta, so the product is evolving
Only suited to repeatable tasks; not a general workflow builder
Each run needs manual review and confirmation before execution

robowork.verdict: No-code platform for building AI agents and automating workflows.
overview: RoboWork is a no-code AI agent and workflow platform that helps businesses automate tasks through conversational agents. Founded in 2025, it lets non-technical users build automations that connect their daily tools. The platform focuses on making agent-based automation practical for small and mid-sized teams.

rootlenses.verdict: AI data intelligence suite with conversational analytics and lifelike voice agents.
overview: Rootlenses is an AI-powered data intelligence suite that lets non-technical users query, visualize and get instant conversational answers from connected data sources. Its Insight module acts like an AI data analyst that securely connects to databases and LLMs to answer questions and generate reports, while its Voice module runs scalable automated calls with lifelike AI voice agents for scheduling, reminders and follow-ups.
pros: No engineering needed for data insights
Combines analytics with voice automation
Scalable outbound calling
cons: Paid only, no public pricing
New product with limited track record

ruflo.verdict: Multi-agent orchestration harness that turns Claude Code into a 100-agent swarm.
overview: Ruflo is an agent harness that wraps Claude Code with swarm coordination, persistent memory, and hundreds of MCP tools. Hooks route tasks automatically while agents share learning across sessions. Formerly known as claude-flow, it is one of the most-starred agent projects on GitHub at around 74k stars.
pros: Enormous capability set out of the box
74k+ stars with relentless development
MIT licensed
cons: Tightly coupled to Claude Code
Complexity can overwhelm solo users
Rebranded from claude-flow — some docs still catching up

runable.verdict: AI agent platform for automating business workflows.
overview: Runable is an AI agent platform for automating business workflows without heavy engineering. Teams describe a task and build agents that carry it out across their tools. It is aimed at operations and business users who want to automate repetitive processes.

runday.verdict: AI sales agents for automated outreach
overview: Runday is a platform for AI sales agents that automate outreach and prospecting workflows. It is a paid product targeting sales teams and agencies. The product is web-based.
pros: Purpose-built for sales
Agent-based automation
cons: Paid only
Limited public detail

runner-h.verdict: H Company's autonomous AI agent that executes complex multi-step online tasks — emails, forms, job applications — by driving websites in real time.
overview: Runner H is the flagship autonomous agent platform from H Company, a European AI lab founded in 2022 and backed by major funding. It takes a single natural-language prompt and orchestrates specialized sub-agents to complete complex multi-step online tasks — sending emails, filling forms, handling job applications, analyzing data and producing content. It is powered by Holo-1, the company's proprietary vision-language model (also open-sourced via Hugging Face), which lets it see and interact with websites in real time rather than relying on APIs. Alongside sibling products Surfer H for web automation and Tester H for software testing, it marks H Company's push from conversational assistants toward execution intelligence, with EU AI Act compliance as a stated differentiator.
pros: Executes real multi-step tasks end to end from one prompt
Own vision model avoids brittle API-only integrations
European company with EU regulatory compliance focus
cons: Relatively new product with a still-maturing ecosystem
Enterprise-grade workflows may require custom pricing
Dependent on browser interaction, so some workflows can be fragile

runsight.verdict: Open-source, self-hosted YAML-first workflow engine for AI agents.
overview: Runsight is an open-source workflow engine that lets developers define AI agent pipelines as plain YAML files committed to Git. A visual canvas writes clean YAML straight to your filesystem, so workflows are diffable, reviewable, and version-controlled like any other code. It tracks per-run cost and latency, enforces hard budget caps, and allows pausing a running agent to fix a prompt without redeploying. Built-in assertions, transform hooks, and regression testing bring engineering rigor to agent development. It's Apache 2.0 licensed and self-hosted, with a quick start via uvx or Docker.
pros: Free and open source under Apache 2.0
Workflows are plain diffable files, not database rows
Runtime intervention: pause, fix, resume live agents
cons: Self-hosted setup required (uvx or Docker)
Developer-focused; not a no-code tool

safestclaw.verdict: OpenClaw alternative that works with no LLM, no API bills, and minimal prompt-injection risk.
overview: SafestClaw reimagines the personal AI assistant without depending on a language model. It uses intent recognition and classic NLP tooling to handle tasks deterministically and offline. The result is a zero-cost, private assistant that stays largely immune to prompt-injection attacks. (Renamed from safeclaw; the old repo URL redirects here.)
pros: $0 running cost — no API keys needed
Near-immune to prompt injection
Works offline on modest hardware
cons: No free-form chat like LLM assistants offer
Deterministic — cannot reason creatively
Smaller project at under 300 stars

sai.verdict: Simular's computer-use agent that runs fleets of autonomous computers in parallel.
overview: Sai, by Simular, is a generally available computer-use agent built around the #SaiFleet concept: instead of one agent on one computer, users deploy fleets of autonomous computers that work in parallel. Sai reads screens, clicks, types, navigates apps, and plans its next move, operating software with no API including legacy desktop apps and logged-in portals. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, on Simular-provisioned cloud VMs or your own device, asks permission on critical actions, and delivers results via iMessage, SMS, or Telegram.
pros: Parallel fleets multiply throughput far beyond one-agent-one-computer
Interface-level operation works where no API exists
Demoed running autonomously for 14 hours on complex tasks
cons: Autonomous control of real computers carries inherent safety risk
Costs scale with fleet size and run time

salt-ai.verdict: Governed AI workflow platform where experts build methods and teams run them from chat.
overview: Salt AI lets domain experts build governed AI workflows on a visual canvas and run them from chat. Builders assemble, test, and version pipelines in plain code, while frontline staff trigger approved methods with one line of text. Every run is recorded step by step with full lineage and audit trails, and it deploys inside your VPC or on-prem.
pros: Designed for regulated, high-compliance industries
Own your methods and data inside your boundary
Audit-ready lineage for every run
cons: Enterprise-focused; no transparent public pricing
Overkill for simple one-off AI experiments

sayora.verdict: AI virtual receptionist for UK small businesses that answers every call 24/7, books jobs into your diary, and texts you the lead.
overview: Sayora is an AI receptionist built in Edinburgh for UK trades and service businesses. It answers calls day and night in a British voice, learns services and prices from the business website, screens spam callers, and books appointments mid-call into a connected calendar. One flat £49-a-month plan covers unlimited minutes with no contract, and callers are told upfront it is AI.
pros: Flat £49/mo with unlimited minutes, no per-minute billing
Live the same day on a month-to-month plan with a 7-day trial
Transparent about AI disclosure, data handling, and limitations
cons: Inbound only — no live call transfers to the owner or staffed fallback.
Early-stage company with no public reviews yet.
UK-focused: UK numbers, UK GDPR framing, and pound pricing.

scalebrowser.verdict: Self-hosted browser infrastructure giving each AI agent its own persistent, human-like browser.
overview: Scalebrowser is self-hosted browser infrastructure that gives each AI agent its own isolated browser with a persistent identity — cookies, logins, passkeys, memory, and tasks survive restarts and moves between machines. A patched Chromium engine, real local GPU values, human-like input, captcha handling, and TOTP/email/SMS code support help agents get through the places where ordinary automation gets blocked. Agents connect over MCP, REST, Node.js, Python, or direct CDP; pricing is based only on concurrent browsers and machines, with unlimited profiles on every plan.
pros: Runs on your own machine instead of a vendor cloud, so sessions and credentials never leave your perimeter.
The patched Chromium works below the page rather than masking automation traces with scripts, beating anti-bot stacks.
Multiple SDKs and MCP support make it pluggable into any agent stack.
cons: Windows 10/11 desktop app with a real GPU required — no hosted mode and no macOS/Linux client.
The 7-day trial requires a payment method up front.

screenpipe.verdict: Local-first recorder that turns your screen and audio history into searchable context for AI agents.
overview: Screenpipe continuously records your screen and audio to build a searchable, AI-powered memory of everything you do on your computer. It is the leading open-source-style alternative to Rewind.ai, Microsoft Recall, Granola and Otter.ai. By default everything stays on your device, and your approved AI agents can query that history through an MCP server or REST API to draft follow-ups, summaries and automations from real work.
pros: Data stays local by default, unlike cloud-based memory tools
Agents can search real work history instead of asking for context
Free tier covers trying local capture, AI search and meeting notes
Inspectable source and self-hostable for privacy-conscious users
cons: Always-on capture costs CPU, battery and disk (roughly 5-10 GB per month)
Source-available under a commercial license, not fully open source
Workplace deployments need employee consent and recording-law review

script-it.verdict: No-code platform for building AI workflows with OCR, speech-to-text, and prompt context management — no coding needed.
overview: Script.it is a no-code platform for building AI workflows without writing code. It bundles advanced OCR and document processing, speech-to-text tooling, and a prompt context management system so users can automate tasks like grading, note-taking, content creation, and marketing analysis. Founder-led live demos show templates such as LinkedIn outreach automation being imported and customized in minutes.
pros: No-code approach with a free plan to start
OCR plus speech-to-text covers document-heavy workflows well
Spoken commands and prompt context management lower the barrier for non-technical users
cons: Could not verify pricing/features on the official homepage (rate-limited during research); details rely on third-party directories
Desktop/mobile platform support claimed by directories looks generic and is unverified

seeclick.verdict: Open-source visual GUI agent that locates interface elements from screenshots.
overview: SeeClick is an open-source visual GUI agent from Nanjing University and Shanghai AI Lab that operates interfaces purely from screenshots. Built on a vision-language model with a dedicated GUI-grounding pretraining strategy, it can locate text, widgets, and icons across mobile, desktop, and web environments. Its ScreenSpot benchmark became the standard test for GUI grounding accuracy.
pros: Research-backed with a published ACL 2024 paper
Foundational for screenshot-based computer-use agents
Open weights and code
cons: Research codebase, not a polished tool
Large model — needs serious GPU
Limited recent development activity

servicenow-ai-agents.verdict: AI agent orchestrator spanning IT, HR, and CRM workflows on the ServiceNow platform.
overview: ServiceNow AI Agents is the agent orchestration layer of the ServiceNow AI Platform, designed to coordinate AI agents that complete end-to-end enterprise workflows across IT, HR, customer service, security, and CRM. Agents operate as digital employees inside ServiceNow's governance framework — a central AI Control Tower gives enterprises transparency, scoped permissions, cost tracking, and auditability over every agent decision. The ecosystem expanded in 2026 with Build Agent (generating full applications from natural language prompts, usable inside Cursor, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot) and specialized security and risk agents. With over 100 billion workflows running on the platform each year and a 98% subscription renewal rate, ServiceNow positions its agents as the governed, enterprise-safe way to deploy autonomous AI.
pros: Enterprise-grade governance unmatched by point solutions
Deep integration with the ServiceNow platform customers already run
Proven scale: 100B+ workflows per year, 98% renewal rate
cons: Requires ServiceNow platform; not standalone
Enterprise pricing and implementation complexity

signalbrain-os.verdict: Experimental deterministic autonomy kernel using topology instead of neural networks for pattern recognition.
overview: SignalBrain-OS is an experimental deterministic autonomy kernel that uses topological data analysis (persistent homology) instead of neural networks for structural pattern recognition. It claims O(1) recall of previously seen patterns via topological fingerprints, fully deterministic same-input-same-output behavior, and edge-native execution with zero cloud dependency. The project publishes proof artifacts, benchmarks, and a companion trust-layer package on PyPI, and is aimed at researchers and developers exploring non-neural AI approaches.

sim-ai.verdict: Visual workspace to build, deploy, and govern AI agents with workflows, knowledge bases, and multi-model support.
overview: Sim is a visual, end-to-end agent builder where developers design AI agent workflows on a canvas, connect models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Ollama, and more) and 60+ integrations, then deploy them through APIs, webhooks, or scheduled jobs. It also adds enterprise governance: access control, spend limits, audit logs, and self-hosting. The core runtime is open source with 18,000+ GitHub stars.
pros: Open-source runtime (18K+ GitHub stars) with self-hosting option
End-to-end platform: build, deploy, monitor, and govern agents in one place
Agent-native observability with per-run tracing and cost tracking
cons: Positioned as an n8n alternative, so switching teams face migration effort
Enterprise governance features likely sit on higher tiers, increasing cost for teams

sim-studio.verdict: Open-source visual workspace for building multi-agent workflows as executable graphs.
overview: Sim Studio is an open-source, Figma-like canvas for designing multi-agent AI workflows as explicit directed graphs. You compose agent blocks with system prompts, tool definitions, and sampling settings, then connect them with conditional, loop, and routing logic — and the graph itself is executable, so you can run simulations to see how prompt or model changes affect outcomes. It supports dozens of pre-built integrations, multiple LLM providers plus local Ollama, and scales from local prototyping to cloud deployment with monitoring and governance.
pros: Apache 2.0 open source with a public GitHub repository
Explicit visual graphs make complex agent logic debuggable
Simulations let you iterate on prompts before production
Local development via Ollama keeps prototyping private and cheap
cons: Young project without a dedicated evaluation framework yet
Workflow-centric; no coding-agent runtime with shell and git primitives
Commercial hosting terms and limits beyond open source are unclear

simplai.verdict: Enterprise agentic AI platform for building and governing AI agents.
overview: SimplAI is a full-stack agentic AI operating system for enterprises, with a no-code studio to build, deploy, and monitor AI agents and multi-agent systems. It supports cloud, on-premise, and air-gapped deployment with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance, 300+ data connectors, and built-in RAG grounding. Pre-built agents cover KYC, AML screening, credit memos, and regulatory reporting for regulated industries.
pros: Enterprise-grade security and governance
Fast PoC-to-production timeline
cons: Custom enterprise pricing, no self-serve

simple-phones.verdict: AI phone agents that answer calls for your business.
overview: Simple Phones provides AI voice agents that answer inbound calls, qualify leads and book appointments for small businesses. Plans run $49 to $97 per month. It is built for service businesses missing calls after hours.
pros: Never miss a call
Simple setup
Good for local businesses
cons: Per-month cost per line
Voice quality varies

simular-pro.verdict: Desktop computer-use AI agent that operates your Mac and browser like a skilled operator.
overview: Simular Pro is a production-grade computer-use agent platform from Simular: instead of wiring APIs, you hand the agent plain instructions and it clicks, types, uploads, and navigates real desktop apps and browsers — processing email, updating CRMs, filling spreadsheets, or running long multi-app workflows. It uses a neuro-symbolic approach (LLMs plus symbolic code and reinforcement learning) so long workflows stay reliable, and every action is visible, inspectable, and editable. Agents can be triggered from existing systems via webhooks, and sister product Sai offers cloud Windows/Linux computers for the same workloads.
pros: Handles messy sites where APIs don't exist
Strong reliability story for long-running workflows
Watch it work live or let it run unattended
cons: Contact-sales positioning; pricing not public
Initial teaching/setup investment required

skene-app.verdict: AI platform that auto-generates onboarding from your codebase and keeps it in sync.
overview: Skene reads a product's codebase and automatically generates role-aware onboarding dashboards, interactive walkthroughs, and documentation tuned to each user's permissions and feature flags. Because it monitors the repository, onboarding content stays in sync with shipped changes without manual updates. Its unusual pricing model charges per completed onboarding rather than per seat, and it also runs automated experiments to improve activation and retention over time.
pros: 5-minute setup with read-only GitHub access
Docs stay current automatically
No per-seat pricing — pay for outcomes
Self-improving growth experiments
cons: Early-stage startup with limited public track record
Needs code access, which some companies won't grant
Niche appeal — mostly indie hackers and PLG startups

skills-sh.verdict: Vercel's free registry of 100,000+ AI agent skills.
overview: Skills.sh is Vercel's open registry of ready-made skills that turn AI coding agents into specialists: install one with a single command and your agent gains proven instructions for UI design, debugging, SEO, testing and more. Skills work across Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, OpenClaw and other agent harnesses. Everything is free, and you can publish your own skills for the community.
pros: Completely free
Huge library
No platform lock-in
cons: Quality varies by skill author

skillsize.verdict: Turn expert methods and frameworks into reusable AI Skills that run across ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot.
overview: Skillsize turns expert methods, frameworks and judgment into executable AI Skills that can analyze, assess, decide and deliver work consistently at scale. Build a skill in Skillsize Studio from your documents and reasoning process, then export it for ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot or as portable Markdown. Work Mode lets you run multiple skills together against a real client brief.
pros: Makes expert methodology portable across AI platforms
Human-in-the-loop review stages for reliability
Targets consultancies and strategy teams directly
cons: No public pricing visible on the site
New product with limited third-party validation

skipcalls.verdict: 24/7 AI receptionist that answers calls, qualifies leads, and books jobs.
overview: SkipCalls is an AI phone-answering service for small businesses that keeps your existing number while an AI agent handles incoming calls and texts. It answers around the clock, qualifies new leads, books appointments straight into your calendar, filters spam, and routes important calls to the right person, sending a concise summary, lead details, and next steps after every call. It integrates with calendars, booking tools, and CRMs like HubSpot, Salesforce, Jobber, and GoHighLevel, and the Android app has 10K+ downloads with a 4.5-star rating.
pros: No per-call or per-minute charges model
Works without changing existing number
Strong integrations for service businesses
cons: Free version is limited
Voice quality and call handling can vary by setup

skydive.verdict: Platform for building AI coworkers that run on their own cloud computers inside your team's tools.
overview: Skydive, built by Anything, lets employees spin up AI agents for growth, engineering, and support work without assembling infrastructure. Each agent runs on its own cloud computer with a browser, file system, and terminal, connects to 600+ integrations like Gmail, GitHub, Notion, and Linear, and can be reached on web, Slack, email, or iMessage. Signup is free and pricing follows model and compute usage, with no seat licenses and no per-agent fees.
pros: No per-seat or per-agent pricing keeps costs tied to actual usage
Employees who know the work can build agents themselves without an AI team
Omnichannel access (Slack, email, iMessage) meets teams where they already work
Backed by Footwork, Bessemer, Uncork, M13, and Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke
cons: Usage-based pricing can be unpredictable for teams with heavy agent workloads
New product (launched August 2026) with a short operational track record
Granting agents broad access to business systems raises oversight and security questions

skygen.verdict: Persistent execution platform for long-horizon AI workflows
overview: Skygen is a persistent execution platform built for long-horizon AI workflows that run for hours or days. It keeps complex, multi-step agent processes alive with durable state, so work survives interruptions instead of timing out. Designed as agent infrastructure for teams running autonomous workflows unattended.
pros: Built specifically for long-horizon agent workloads
Prevents workflow timeouts on extended runs
cons: Paid only
Niche infrastructure play, not a consumer tool

skyvern.verdict: AI agents that automate workflows natively inside any website's browser
overview: Skyvern runs browser automation the way a person would, reading pages with computer vision and following plain-language instructions to complete multi-step web tasks. It can log into portals, pull invoices, fill out forms, handle CAPTCHAs and 2FA, and extract structured data without fragile selector-based scripts. The product targets operations teams and developers, with cloud runs, self-hosted Docker options, Python and TypeScript SDKs, and integrations with automation tools like Zapier, n8n, and Clay.
pros: Open source (AGPL-3.0) with 23k+ GitHub stars
Survives website UI changes automatically
SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliant
Works behind logins without APIs
cons: Paid cloud plans for hosted usage
Browser automation depends on task reliability at scale

smythos.verdict: Open-source operating system for building and deploying AI agents.
overview: SmythOS is an open-source platform for creating AI agents with a visual builder and runtime. Developers design agent workflows and deploy them without managing infrastructure. Being MIT-licensed, teams can self-host and customize it freely.

snaplogic.verdict: Enterprise integration platform with 1,000+ connectors, SnapGPT copilot and no-code AgentCreator.
overview: SnapLogic is an enterprise integration platform unifying data integration, application integration and API management in one visual low-code environment. It ships 1,000+ prebuilt Snaps connectors, a SnapGPT generative-AI copilot that translates business intent into pipelines, and AgentCreator for building no-code AI agents on top of enterprise data. The platform is MCP-native so agents and pipelines can function as governed MCP endpoints.
pros: One platform covering data, apps, APIs and AI agents
MCP-native design suits the agentic enterprise trend
Strong visual tooling with AI copilot for faster pipeline building
Enterprise security, masking and policy enforcement built in
cons: Enterprise-focused custom pricing with no entry-level plans
Overkill for small teams with simple integration needs
Agentic features add another layer of complexity to govern

springbase.verdict: AI productivity OS with reusable prompt recipes and scheduled agents.
overview: Springbase (formerly Springhub) is a productivity OS where your best prompts become reusable Recipes that run on demand or on schedule. It bundles 350+ text and image models including GPT, Claude and Gemini in one interface, connects to 1,000+ apps like Gmail, Notion, Slack and GitHub, and grounds answers in your uploaded documents with citations. Scheduled agents handle recurring work like briefings and reports without manual prompting.
pros: Free plan available
No switching between AI tools
Real task execution, not just chat

stack-ai.verdict: Enterprise no-code platform for building secure AI agents and workflows on private company data.
overview: Stack AI is a no-code platform that lets teams build AI agents and workflows on enterprise data — knowledge bases like SharePoint, Confluence and Google Drive — and publish them as chat assistants, forms or APIs into Slack, Teams, Salesforce and HubSpot. It emphasizes enterprise readiness: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, PII masking, guardrails and evaluations, with model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or local LLMs. A free plan offers 500 runs/month; scaling happens on custom enterprise pricing.
pros: Strong G2 reviews for ease of use and fast deployment without heavy coding
Serious compliance story: SSO, RBAC, audit logs, PII masking, data residency
Hands-on pilot engagement with dedicated AI specialists praised by customers
cons: Learning curve for advanced use and occasional performance inconsistencies reported
Pricing concerns for small teams; scale pricing is custom and opaque

stage5.verdict: AI site agent that turns construction crews' WhatsApp chatter into official paperwork.
overview: Stage5 puts an AI agent inside the WhatsApp and Telegram groups construction crews already use, and turns their chatter into the paperwork the business runs on. Foremen send photos of delivery notes or voice notes; Stage5 transcribes, understands, and files everything into a self-writing daily site journal, matched supplier invoices, and a document inbox the office opens each morning. Integrations with Monday.com, Google Drive, SharePoint, and 70+ tools keep systems in sync. It's already live with production customers and positions itself as the system of record for construction projects.
pros: No new app for field crews to learn
Journal entries marked as missing are never invented
Honest feature-status labeling (live/beta/preview)
cons: Niche: built specifically for construction workflows
Pricing not published

starnus.verdict: Autonomous AI sales employee that runs outbound prospecting, outreach, and follow-ups on autopilot.
overview: Starnus is an AI platform that runs outbound sales end to end for founders and B2B teams. It reads your website to build an ideal customer profile in about 30 seconds, then finds and enriches matching leads, drafts personalized email and LinkedIn outreach, and executes week-by-week plans with your approval. You review the plan once a week while its specialized agents handle sourcing, sending, follow-ups, and reporting.
pros: Replaces a stack of data, enrichment, and sending tools
No technical setup or workflow building required
Approval-based execution keeps you in control
Founder-friendly self-serve model
cons: Pricing isn't published on the homepage
Autonomous outreach needs review to protect sender reputation
Focused on outbound only, not inbound

steel-browser.verdict: Open-source headless browser API purpose-built for AI agents, with session management and observability.
overview: Steel is an open-source browser API designed specifically for AI agents. It lets you spin up fleets of managed Chromium sessions in the cloud and control them via API or SDKs, handling the painful parts of web automation — JavaScript rendering, logins, proxies, CAPTCHAs, anti-bot measures and scaling — so agents can focus on the task. Agent-focused observability like live session viewers, replays and step-by-step agent logs makes failed runs far easier to debug.
pros: Open-source (Apache 2.0) and self-hostable — audit exactly what runs
Built from day one for agent workloads: fast session starts, agent logs, replays
Standard CDP/Playwright/Puppeteer/Selenium connections — no lock-in
Built-in stealth, CAPTCHA solving and token-optimized page formats
cons: Early-stage company with a smaller team and less enterprise track record
Fewer built-in integrations beyond the core CDP/Playwright/Selenium layer
Self-hosting the open-source version requires browser infrastructure know-how

stewai.verdict: Marketplace of pre-tested AI workflow recipes that plug into Claude and ChatGPT to handle demanding tasks with fewer agent tokens.
overview: StewAI offers hundreds of ready-to-run 'recipes' — executable AI workflows with fixed inputs, steps, checks, and outputs — that AI agents can call through a plugin or MCP integration. Recipes cover research and specialized methods; when none fits, an agent can build and test a private one. Sign-in is by email with no API key, and recipe runs cost credits.
pros: Tested, reusable workflows cut repeated agent planning
Works inside existing agents rather than replacing them
